data.title: Rate
data.tagline: Express a rating with stars or ordered levels
data.description: A rating control lets people show satisfaction on an ordered scale, often with five stars. Pair the graphic with a readable number or label, and make sure keyboard and screen-reader users can select a value too.

avoid: Use stars when the levels have no shared meaning
Rely on color alone to show the selected value
Hide what the first and last levels mean
Make a rating required without explaining why

lessonPractice.title: After an order, the product collects satisfaction from 1 to 5 and users must understand their current selection. How should it work?

options.label: Use a five-level rating control and also show readable text such as Selected 4 of 5
options.feedback: The control expresses ordered levels, while text makes the current value available without relying only on stars or color.

options.label: Replace it with Satisfied and Dissatisfied buttons and remove the middle levels
options.feedback: A binary choice captures positive or negative sentiment but loses the five degrees required by this task.

options.label: Use a regular number field and allow any decimal value from 1 to 5
options.feedback: Free numbers can exceed the rating rules and do not provide the fixed levels and immediate feedback of a rating control.

data.agentPrompt: Use a 1–5 rating control for product feedback, show its value in text, and support keyboard input. Preserve the existing rule for half ratings, then test unrated, selected, and read-only aggregate states.
